questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the efficient subsidy for a positive externality
questions.stem: A software team's ticket proposes paying developers for documenting internal APIs. Which policy best corrects the positive externality?

options.text: A per-unit subsidy equal to the marginal external benefit at the efficient quantity
A tax on API calls to reduce congestion
options.misconception: confuses a positive externality with a negative one

options.text: No intervention because private markets always reach efficiency
options.misconception: ignores that external benefits cause underproduction

options.text: A per-unit subsidy equal to the marginal external benefit at the efficient quantity
options.misconception: treats the subsidy as a lump-sum transfer rather than per-unit

questions.explanation: A per-unit subsidy aligns private and social marginal benefit. A tax or no intervention leaves output below the efficient level.
questions.hint: Match the subsidy to the external benefit at efficiency.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how cap and trade achieves efficiency
questions.stem: Ticket 7 asks why a cap-and-trade system can reach the same efficient outcome as a tax. Explain briefly.

answer.exemplar: A cap sets total emissions and trading moves permits to firms with the lowest abatement cost, so aggregate reduction is achieved at minimum total cost, matching an efficient tax outcome.

questions.explanation: Trading reallocates abatement to low-cost firms. The cap fixes quantity while the market finds the least-cost allocation.
questions.hint: The cap fixes quantity; trade finds lowest cost.

questions.hint: Lower cost for same reduction wins.

questions.learningObjective: Explain Coase irrelevance of initial allocation
questions.stem: Ticket 248 asks whether the initial rights assignment affects the final efficient outcome under Coase. Does it?

options.text: Yes, efficiency requires rights to the victim
Yes, efficiency requires rights to the polluter
options.misconception: efficiency is independent of initial rights

options.text: No, the final allocation is efficient either way; only distribution changes
Only if transaction costs are high

questions.explanation: With low transaction costs, bargaining reaches efficiency regardless of initial rights; only who pays changes.

questions.stem: Ticket 263 asks who benefits from a subsidy on a positive externality. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Both producers and consumers benefit: producers receive a higher effective price and consumers pay a lower price, while output rises toward efficiency.

questions.explanation: The subsidy splits between producers and consumers through price changes, expanding output.

questions.learningObjective: Explain permit price as marginal abatement cost
questions.stem: Ticket 278 asks what the permit price represents in equilibrium. Explain.

answer.exemplar: In equilibrium the permit price equals the marginal abatement cost, so firms abate until their marginal cost matches the price.
